h1:
A Ranong Photo Trip
Grass Hill · Koh Phayam · Old Town · Hot Springs
intro: Ranong gives you several completely different looks in one trip: open grassland on the hills with a full 360° view, the clear water of Koh Phayam, a Sino-Portuguese old town with vintage shop signs, and natural hot springs set in a garden. This is a 3-day, 2-night plan that orders each stop to hit it when the light is good — not at noon when harsh sun flattens everything.

blocks.html: Ranong is known as the city of eight months of rain and four of sun — the sky changes fast, which actually works in a photographer's favour because you get dramatic morning clouds and golden evening light. This plan centres on four spots: the Grass Hill, Koh Phayam, the old town in the city, and Raksawarin hot springs — then times each one to land in the light that shoots best.

blocks.text: The 4 main photo spots this plan covers

items.name: Grass Hill (Khao Hua Lan)
items.blurb: Grassland on low rolling hills with almost no tall trees to block the view — walk to the top and you get a full 360°. In the rainy season the grass turns deep green; in the dry season it goes golden. Early mornings bring thin mist drifting along the ridges. Just 5–10 minutes from town.
items.meta: Open access · no entry fee · on Phetkasem Rd toward Chumphon

items.name: Koh Phayam
items.blurb: An island with no cars — motorbikes and three-wheelers do the work. White sand and clear water, with standouts like the Hin Talu rock arch at Ao Khao Khwai, a pair of rock formations curving toward each other that's a popular check-in spot. About 45 minutes by speedboat from Pak Nam pier.

items.name: Old town (Ranong Old Town)
items.blurb: Sino-Portuguese buildings and old wooden houses in the city centre, vintage shop signs, peeling painted walls with a story behind them. There's Tian Sue Mansion (Baan Fa Prathan), a century-old Chinese house with beautifully carved doors and windows. Good shooting throughout the whole district.
items.meta: Free to wander · cafés along the way

items.name: Raksawarin hot springs
items.blurb: Natural hot springs in a public park in the middle of town — hot mineral water with no sulphur smell, and steam rising to use as a backdrop. Free foot-soaking, with a small fee if you want a full soak.
items.meta: Foot soak free · full soak ~40–50 THB · open morning–evening

blocks.title: What to know about light before you set the schedule
blocks.html: The Grass Hill shoots best in the early morning and in the evening light, because midday sun is harsh and makes the grassland look flat. The old town is best early before the crowds, or under overcast light. So this plan puts the Grass Hill in the late afternoon on day one and saves the old town for the morning.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrive in Ranong, shoot the old town, finish on the Grass Hill

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Old town + hot springs + Grass Hill in evening light

items.activity: Arrive in Ranong town, check in at a place in the city
items.note: Staying in the city centre makes it easy to walk the old town and reach the hot springs

items.activity: Lunch in town, then wander the old town
items.note: The sun softens a bit around now, so vintage shop signs and old walls shoot easily

items.activity: Stop at Tian Sue Mansion (Baan Fa Prathan), an old Chinese house with beautiful carvings
items.note: The carved wooden doors and windows are great for detail shots

items.activity: Head to Raksawarin hot springs, soak your feet, shoot the steam
items.note: Foot soaking is free; a full soak costs around 40–50 THB extra

items.activity: Go up the Grass Hill for evening light and sunset
items.note: Only 5–10 minutes' drive from town — wear easy walking shoes, the slopes get slippery when the grass is wet
Ranong has plenty of seafood and bold southern Thai food to choose from

blocks.text: Day 2 — Cross to Koh Phayam, stay the night by the sea

blocks.html: Today you shift base to Koh Phayam. The pier is at Pak Nam Ranong — turn into the lane beside the Pak Nam police station and go about 1 km. Speedboats run several times a day, morning to afternoon, taking around 45 minutes. Book a morning departure so you have a full day on the island. There are no cars on the island, so renting a motorbike to ride around yourself is the easiest way to get about.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Koh Phayam — white sand, the rock arch, sunset over the sea

items.activity: Go to Pak Nam pier, take the morning speedboat to Koh Phayam
items.note: Boat fare around 350 THB/trip — get to the pier 20–30 minutes before departure

items.activity: Arrive on the island, check in at a beachfront place, rent a motorbike
items.note: The island runs on motorbikes and three-wheelers — fill up the tank before heading out

items.activity: Ride around shooting the white sand, clear water, and coconut palms along the beach
items.note: Morning light is still soft, so the sea photographs clearer than at midday

items.activity: Lunch at a beachfront restaurant, then hide from the afternoon sun
items.note: The afternoon sun is harsh — save your energy for the evening shoot

items.activity: Head to the Hin Talu rock arch at Ao Khao Khwai, shoot the curved rocks
items.note: Free to visit — check the tide schedule first; at some tides you can walk right up to the rocks for a better shot

items.activity: Find a spot on the west-facing beach for sunset over the sea
items.note: Koh Phayam faces out to the Andaman, so you get the full sunset right over the water

blocks.text: Day 3 — Shoot the island in the morning, cross back, finish in town

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Koh Phayam in the morning, back to the mainland, more of the city

items.activity: Wake early to shoot the beach in soft light, before people head down
items.note: Early morning the beach is quiet — you get empty-beach shots with no one walking through

items.activity: Return the motorbike, pack up, take the mid-morning speedboat back to Ranong
items.note: Check the return boat times in advance — off-season some departures may be cancelled

items.activity: Reach the mainland, stop at Rattanarangsan Palace (replica)
items.note: A cluster of wooden buildings on a hill — free to walk around outside and take in the town view

items.activity: Lunch in town, find a café in the Rueang Rat area to rest
items.note: The Rueang Rat area has nicely decorated cafés to shoot before you head home
Popular Ranong souvenirs are cashew nuts and processed seafood

blocks.text: A checklist of what to pack for photographers

items: Power bank and spare camera batteries — power is limited at some spots on Koh Phayam, so charge everything full before crossing over
Lens cloth — Ranong is humid, and steam at the hot springs plus sea spray fog up a lens easily
Easy walking shoes — the Grass Hill is a grassy slope that gets slippery when wet, so sneakers beat sandals
A waterproof bag or phone pouch — handy on the speedboat and when shooting near the water
An umbrella or light rain jacket — Ranong's sky changes fast, with drizzle possible in any season

blocks.title: Which time of year shoots best
blocks.html: In the rainy season (May–October) the Grass Hill is at its greenest with the best clouds, but the sea is rough and some boats are cancelled. In the dry season (November–April) the sea is clear and calm, ideal for crossing to Koh Phayam, but the grass on the hills runs more golden than green. Choose based on the look you're after.

faq.q: When should I shoot the Ranong Grass Hill?
faq.a: It shoots best in the early morning when thin mist is still drifting, and in the evening light before sunset. Midday sun is harsh and flattens the grassland. In the rainy season the grass is deep green; in the hot season it goes golden — pick the tone you want.

faq.q: How long is the boat to Koh Phayam, and how much is it?
faq.a: It's about 45 minutes by speedboat from Pak Nam Ranong pier, with a fare of around 350 THB per trip. There are several departures from morning to afternoon — check the schedule and book ahead, especially off-season when some runs may be cancelled.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Raksawarin hot springs?
faq.a: Entering the park and soaking your feet is free. A full-body soak in the service pools costs a small fee of around 40–50 THB per person. The water here is hot mineral water with no sulphur smell.

faq.q: How many days is enough for a Ranong photo trip?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is just right — you can cover the Grass Hill, the old town, and the in-town hot springs, plus stay one night on Koh Phayam to shoot the sea sunset and the beach in the morning. If you only have two days, skip the overnight on the island and do it as a day trip.

faq.q: Where is Ranong's old town, and can you walk around it?
faq.a: It's in central Ranong and free to explore on foot, with Sino-Portuguese buildings, old wooden houses, vintage shop signs, and the old Chinese Tian Sue Mansion to shoot — plus nicely decorated cafés in the Rueang Rat area to rest along the way.
